These declines were primarily driven by higher deposit costs, which were partially offset by higher asset yields and increased net interest income from Global Markets activity.

comparisons.peer_topic: Asset Sensitivity and Market Drivers of Wealth Management Net Interest Income
comparisons.peer_summary: The Wealth Management balance sheet is asset sensitive, meaning net interest income increases in higher rate environments and decreases in lower ones, as assets reprice faster than liabilities. Changes in interest rates may also affect deposit levels due to competition and impact client loan demand, contributing to a decrease in net interest income sensitivity at December 31, 2024, compared to the prior year due to shifts in the asset/liability mix and market rates.
comparisons.comparison: While Citi focuses on the realized performance outcome where higher Markets NIM drove margin improvement, Morgan Stanley discusses the structural sensitivity of its Wealth Management balance sheet to interest rates, noting it is asset-sensitive. This provides context for how net interest income might behave in rising rate environments, contrasting with Citi's specific attribution of margin growth to Markets activity rather than general balance sheet sensitivity dynamics.

sentences.text: Citi's net interest margin was 2.42% on a taxable equivalent basis in the fourth quarter of 2024, an increase of nine basis points from the prior quarter, largely driven by higher Markets net interest margin.
